ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DEC$, we have $AB=DE$, $AC=DC$, $CE=CB$. Point $E$ is on $AB$. If $\angle ACE=2\angle ECB=50^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle A$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle ACE = 2\angle ECB = 50^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ECB = 25^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ACB = \angle ACE + \angle ECB = 50^\circ + 25^\circ = 75^\circ$,\\
since $CE = CB$, $\angle ECB = 25^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle B = \angle CEB = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - \angle ECB) = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - 25^\circ) = 77.5^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle A = 180^\circ - \angle B - \angle ACB = 180^\circ - 77.5^\circ - 75^\circ = \boxed{27.5^\circ}$.

Also because CE = CB, triangle CEB is an isosceles triangle, whose vertex angle ∠ECB = 25°, so the base angles ∠CEB = ∠EBC = (180° - 25°)/2 = 77.5°. Since A, E, B are collinear, ray BE is in the same direction as BA, therefore ∠ABC = ∠EBC = 77.5°. In triangle ABC, ∠A = 180° - ∠ACB - ∠ABC = 180° - 75° - 77.5° = 27.5°.
